items.question: How carefully must this teaching be concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains unworthy people
items.inference: This teaching should be guarded with effort among the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching be transmitted after proper testing?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of the Kaula doctrine become known?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The Kaula determination is now known
items.inference: The speaker knows the determination of the Kaula doctrine through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the soul that is declared, and what is its essential nature?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both the identity and the essential nature of the declared soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what complete explanation should be given?
premises: The soul's dissolution is questioned
The locus of dissolution is unknown
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker asks to be told fully into what the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme and partless qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme
That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The reality in question is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified as haṃsa and as the individual of power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is also the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual associated with power.
uncertainties: The precise sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.

items.question: Where does the breath-filled vital air abide within all living beings?
premises: Vital air is filled with breath
All beings are the locus considered
That air is situated within them
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the physical body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
The moment of leaving is decisive
A supreme designation is applied
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is the traditionally transmitted teaching heard within the ear?
premises: Something is heard in the ear
The goddess is addressed
The teaching comes through traditional succession
items.inference: The teaching transmitted through tradition is heard as abiding in the ear.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect arises from merely hearing this knowledge, O fair-faced one?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing itself is the means
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.

items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is undertaken for six months
The practitioner attains an ochre state
That state is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.

items.plain_english: whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What freedom and companionship result from this sustained spiritual practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
Association with yogis is attained
Union with them is achieved
items.inference: The practitioner is freed from all diseases and gains union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What practice concerning the soul has now been fully explained to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
The teaching concerns practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the recipient
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given

The recipient has firm resolve

items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has made a firm resolve.

items.question: Why must the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued
It originates from the yoginīs
Transmission of it is prohibited
items.inference: The Kaula essence, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: How has the body become pure after being struck by the veil of ignorance?
premises: The body was struck by ignorance
A change is declared today
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: The speaker declares that her body, once struck by ignorance, is now pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, though it was once struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish now
The topic is overcoming time
The desired teaching is auspicious
items.inference: The speaker wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: How can death be destroyed without any doubt according to this teaching?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is no doubt in the teaching
Death can be destroyed
items.inference: The teacher asserts without doubt the means by which death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: Why does even a wise person burn at the tip of nectar by its essence?
premises: The tip of nectar is involved

items.plain_english: Even a wise person burns at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: How should the breath be drawn slowly at the root of the tongue and palate?
premises: The practice is located at tongue and palate root
The breath is prepared and drawn in
The action must be done slowly

items.plain_english: Having fixed attention at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows when this breath practice is maintained for one year?
premises: The practice is performed for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this method destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
